reviewKind: independent transaction review of compiler-owned outbox storage foundation
settingsEvidence: Explicitly inherited user-confirmed Sol/high batch; no settings changed.
scope: delivery_outbox.ts, its lexical inclusion inside createPersistenceClient, and the three generated-host storage tests. Review atomic mutation/intent storage, duplicate/version/key/payload invariants, per-key commit order and current storage limits. No declarations, worker, scheduler or 18-case conformance approval.

findings.finding: Enqueue checks a permanently captured transactional boolean, not whether the source transaction is still active. A host callback can retain its transaction client, let the generated outer transaction commit, then enqueue through that retained client. On SQLite this succeeds with inTransaction=false: schema/key/sequence/intent statements autocommit independently. The primitive therefore does not enforce its claimed same-source-transaction boundary for every client it permits to enqueue. Captured views also retain the boolean, and retry attempts have no explicit capability invalidation.
findings.reproduction: In a tiny in-memory SQLite harness, extract the actual emitted createPersistenceClient wrappers and transaction method from target.rs, include the unmodified delivery_outbox.ts, and capture tx inside root.transaction. After that method commits, call captured.enqueue_delivery_intent for revision 2. SQLite reports no transaction before or after the call, yet root.read_delivery_intent finds the new durable row. A direct outbox-inclusion probe independently reproduces the same result.
findings.requiredCorrection: Bind enqueue authority to a live source transaction/attempt token shared across its views and invalidate it when the source transaction commits or rolls back. A stale client must not become valid merely because an unrelated later transaction uses the same SQLite connection. Add retained-client rejection after COMMIT and ROLLBACK, and after retry retirement, with no key-sequence or intent writes. Preserve nested savepoint behavior within a still-live outer boundary.
findings.exposureLimit: Currently a generated-host API misuse path, not an authored-language or public HTTP exploit. Compiler-owned host integration still needs to enforce this core storage boundary before broader bindings rely on it. PostgreSQL retained-client behavior was not executed by this reviewer.

findings.finding: Array.map skips holes, so sparse payload arrays bypass the recursive rejection of unsupported values. JSON.stringify then replaces each hole with null. Enqueueing Array(1) stores [null], and a later same-identity enqueue with payload [null] is accepted as identical. In contrast, the dense array [undefined] correctly faults. This silently rewrites an unsupported payload and aliases two distinct host inputs at the immutable-payload equality boundary.
findings.reproduction: Run the unmodified outbox include against in-memory SQLite inside BEGIN/COMMIT. Enqueue revision 3 with Array(1), then enqueue the same identity with [null]. Both return the same intent ID and stored [null]. The negative [undefined] probe raises delivery.payload.
findings.requiredCorrection: Reject holes and other unsupported array shapes before canonical serialization, or define and enforce a reviewed typed normalization that makes this equivalence intentional. Add sparse-array versus explicit-null and dense-undefined cases, and preserve canonical equivalence for valid object key reorderings.
findings.exposureLimit: Payload is currently unknown at the host primitive boundary. Future checked compiler payload bindings must still enforce exact typed payload/version contracts; this finding does not claim authored code can currently construct a sparse delivery payload.

independentProbes.limits: Uses real SQLite and exact emitted transaction branch/include with dependency helpers supplied by the harness. It is not a separately compiled application, PostgreSQL probe or full runtime suite. No source or build files were created.

reviewedWithoutAdditionalFinding: During a live source transaction the include closes over exactly that client's PostgreSQL/SQLite adapter and deadline wrappers. It does not open a separate database connection or commit an intent independently.

The three storage tests cover mutation plus intent success, outer rollback leaving no row/intent/change revision, rejection on the root nontransactional client, stable ID/version/payload through a fresh process, sequential duplicate equivalence, immutable mismatch rejection and same-key serialization through source commit.

For a valid compiler-created schema and default READ COMMITTED PostgreSQL transactions, key-row insertion/update locks serialize same-job/key enqueues through COMMIT. SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE provides adapter-wide write serialization. Later same-key enqueues allocate their sequence only after the earlier transaction releases its lock.

Logical source identity and per-key sequence have database uniqueness constraints. Sequential duplicate enqueue returns the existing ID and leaves its immutable payload/version/key unchanged. A concurrent inconsistent-key duplicate remains constrained by source-identity uniqueness even though its key locks differ; its exact fault mapping is not independently exercised here.

Sequence allocation uses database BIGINT arithmetic, an explicit maximum guard and TEXT casts at the driver boundary, avoiding JavaScript integer precision as ordering authority. Ordering uses key_sequence rather than enqueue timestamps.

Rollback removes key/sequence/intent writes with the source transaction, and committed rows are durable rather than depending on an in-memory wakeup. Existing TX-001 acknowledged/unknown commit rules continue to apply; this include adds no external dispatch or blind replay path.

Valid plain-object payloads are serialized deterministically with sorted keys; unsupported values, nonfinite numbers, cycles and non-plain object values are rejected by the inspected canonicalizer. The sparse-array exception is recorded above.

mainReportedEvidence.limits: Attributed to the main, not independently rerun. No saved focused log/revision hash was supplied with this handoff. These generated-host cases do not certify a public job boundary or the 18-case ASYNC catalog. Reviewer ran no broad build while readiness implementation was active.

schemaBackendAndCollisionLimits: Schema is created lazily by the first transactional enqueue. Reading before those tables exist is not an empty-queue proof; it faults at SQL execution. Startup/migration ownership remains to be implemented before a worker expects an initialized queue.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS does not attest the columns, primary keys, unique constraints or checks of pre-existing tables. Current correctness assumes the two reserved compiler-owned tables have the exact v1 layout. Compatibility/version migration and collision handling are not established by the three tests.

The source-identity read treats exactly one existing row as a duplicate; it does not explicitly reject more than one row before trying a new insert. Under the required unique schema this is unreachable; a collision/corrupt layout must not be treated as supported storage.

Adapter selection assumes one configured database. The include selects SQLite whenever postgres is null; missing both adapters is not explicitly normalized by the include. No two-adapter or adapter-failover atomicity is claimed.

UUID primary-key collision is fail-closed through SQL constraints, but collision fault injection/recovery is unexecuted. Sequence exhaustion is guarded, not independently exercised here. Long identity/payload limits, depth limits and restored-record validation remain unspecified at this host-only boundary.

Same-key ordering is scoped to (job, ordering_key). Cross-job/global order, different-key writer parallelism, worker claim/dispatch FIFO and terminal/unknown key release are not established by storage insertion order.
futureCompilerAndWorkerGates: The primitive accepts host-supplied job/sourceOperation/entity/entityId/revision/version/key strings. No authored job declaration can currently invoke or forge them. This is not yet proof that future compiler bindings derive identity from checked source mutations, validate payload contracts, or restrict storage/operator authority.

No durable claim/fence, dispatch checkpoint, attempt history, cancellation transition, receipt/ack, scheduler, continuation, retention or replay implementation is approved. A pending state vocabulary and immutable row do not implement those contracts.

Concurrent same-revision duplicates, incompatible ordering-key races, aborted first allocator, cross-process commit-order races, lease/effect crash traces and version-handler behavior remain required at the appropriate generated boundary.
The ASYNC 18-case catalog remains contract-only. RM-306/RM-307 and golden integration retain their full execution and independent review gates.
reviewGate: Resolve the two reproduced findings and obtain independent correction review of exact resulting bytes before approving this storage foundation. Preserve host-only/schema/backend limits and do not close RM-306 or claim worker/18-case conformance from the foundation tests.
